const _extendedEmailProtocol = edit(/(?:mailto:email|xmpp:email(?:\/[A-Za-z0-9@.]+)?)/)
  .replace(/email/g, _extendedEmail)
  .getRegex();

/**
 * Normal Inline Grammar

const inlineNormal = {
  _backpedal: noopTest, // only used for GFM url
  anyPunctuation,
  autolink,
  blockSkip,
  br,
  code: inlineCode,
  del: noopTest,
  delLDelim: noopTest,
  delRDelim: noopTest,
  emStrongLDelim,
  emStrongRDelimAst,
  emStrongRDelimUnd,
  escape,
  link,
  nolink,
  punctuation,
  reflink,
  reflinkSearch,
  tag,
  text: inlineText,
  url: noopTest,
};

type InlineKeys = keyof typeof inlineNormal;

/**
 * Pedantic Inline Grammar
 */

const inlinePedantic: Record<InlineKeys, RegExp> = {
  ...inlineNormal,
  emStrongLDelim: emStrongLDelimPedantic,
  emStrongRDelimAst: emStrongRDelimAstPedantic,
  emStrongRDelimUnd: emStrongRDelimUndPedantic,
  link: edit(/^!?\[(label)\]\((.*?)\)/)
    .replace('label', _inlineLabel)
    .getRegex(),
  reflink: edit(/^!?\[(label)\]\s*\[([^\]]*)\]/)
    .replace('label', _inlineLabel)
    .getRegex(),
};

 * GFM Inline Grammar
 */

  emStrongRDelimAst: emStrongRDelimAstGfm,

content.text: The bug is fixed. A code span's backslash no longer hides its closing backtick from the emphasis pass, so both reported cases now render as expected. **Cause:** In `src/Lexer.ts`, inline parsing first builds a masked copy of the source where escapes like `\*` are replaced by filler characters, so emphasis can't match inside them. That step masked every `\` followed by punctuation, including the `\`` in `` `C:\Users\` ``. The closing backtick vanished from the masked copy, so the later code-span mask paired the wrong backticks. The text between `` `C:\Users\` `` and the next code span, `**home**` included, was treated as code, and emphasis was skipped. **Fix:** - `src/rules.ts`: added an `escapeOutsideCode` pattern that matches a code span or an escape, whichever comes first, and added it to the inline grammar. The existing `anyPunctuation` is unchanged because the tokenizer uses it for link and title unescaping. - `src/Lexer.ts`: the masking step now uses that pattern and only fills in matches that are escapes. Code spans are left intact, and the length-preserving mask is unchanged. **Verification:** - Both examples from the report now render as expected. `` `a\` *b* `c` `` gives `a\ b c`. - `npm run test:specs`: 1911 pass, 0 fail (1909 existing plus 2 new). - `npm run test:unit`: 199 pass, 0 fail. - A 8000-span backslash-and-backtick input parses in about 26 ms. **Added:** `test/specs/new/codespan_backslash_emphasis.md` and `.html`, covering the two reported cases and a `` `a\*` `` case. **Not verified:** - Lint: I tried `npx eslint` on the two changed files, but the command was denied, so it has not been run. - `npm run build:esbuild` regenerated `lib/` (the `marked.esm.js` and `marked.umd.js` bundles, with maps). I did not check whether `lib/` existed before, so you may see it in `git status`. I did not commit anything.
